```text
Ogre Treasure
Ogres don’t keep valuables or interesting items,
but are often unaware when they swallow such
things. Characters searching a giant mound of ogre
excrement might discover something interesting if
they can stomach sifting through the stinking mess.

---

Fecal Mound Discoveries
d20 Discovery
1 An art object or piece of jewelry worth 3d6 ss
2 A tool or set of tools worth 1 gc or less
3 A pouch containing 2d6 cp
4 A set of filthy fine clothes
5 A suit of mail
6 A military melee weapon
7 A small chest containing 3d6 ss
8 An intact halfling corpse
9 A Size 1/2 stone idol
10 A small bottle containing a healing potion
11 An unconscious shepherd (as commoner)
12 A bundle of 1d6 arrows or bolts
13 A silver serving platter worth 1d6 + 2 ss
14 A bottle of spirits
15 A stained, sodden book containing an
incantation of a rank 1 spell
16 1d6 Void larvae
17 2d6 bricks
18 1 interesting thing (physical objects only)
19 1 jewel worth 1 gc
20 1 enchanted object
Customizing Ogres
As noted above, ogres display great variety in form,
capabilities, and behavior. You can customize the
basic ogre into your own unique creation by applying
any of the following modifications to its statistics box.
Flatulent
Many ogres suffer from incredible flatulence and their
rumbling guts expel blasts of foul-smelling gas from
their bowels with alarming force and regularity. The
build-up of gases and excrement sometimes make
defeating them just as punishing as fighting them.
Health Reduce by 10.
Fetid Wind When the ogre takes damage, roll a d6. On a 4
or higher, the ogre noisily breaks wind. Target one Size 3
space adjacent to the ogre’s space. Each creature in the
space makes a Strength challenge roll. On a failure, the
creature becomes Diseased until the end of their next turn.
Empty Bowels When the ogre becomes injured, it voids its
bowels. Target one Size 3 space adjacent to the ogre’s
space. Hot, stinking feces forms covers the ground in the
space with difficult terrain. A creature in the space makes
an Agility challenge roll. On a failure, the creature becomes
Blinded until the end of its next turn and Diseased for 1
minute.
Explosive End When the ogre’s damage total reaches its
Health score, it explodes to throw chunks of meat and blood
splashing across everything within 3 yards of the ogre’s
space. A creature in the area makes an Agility challenge
roll. On a failure, the creature takes 1d6 damage, moves 1d3
yards away from the ogre’s space, and falls prone.
Infested
As ogres tend not to be selective when it comes to
what they put in their mouths, they are prone to
picking up all kinds of parasites, which then multiply
in their guts. Infested ogres show their sickness in
their poor color and unusual thinness.
Health Reduce by 10.
Infected Vomit A creature that takes damage from the ogre’s
Vomit makes a Strength challenge roll. On a failure, the
creature reduces its Health by 2d6 and becomes Diseased
for 24 hours. While the creature has this affliction, it takes
1d6 extra damage each time it takes damage
Mutant
The troll magic responsible for ogres’ existence makes
them prone to mutation. Many ogres display an
unusual physical characteristic.
Insanity —
Frightening A creature not immune to the Frightened
affliction makes attack rolls against the ogre with 1 bane.
Mutation The ogre has one mutation. Roll a d20 and find the
result on the Ogre Mutations table.

---

Ogre Mutations
d20 Mutation
1 The ogre has strangely colored or patterned skin.
2 The ogre’s head is far too big for its body.
3 The ogre has an enormous sexual organ.
4 The ogre has a horn growing out from the side of its
head.
5 The ogre has one enormous and one tiny arm.
6 The ogre’s skin is covered in weeping pustules.
7 The ogre has just one eye in the center of its head.
8 Thick fur covers the ogre’s body.
9 The ogre has enormous hands and feet.
10 The ogre has a second face in its abdomen.
11 The ogre has a weird fin growing out from the
center of its back.
12 The ogre has duck feet.
13 The ogre has scales on its neck and shoulders.
14 The ogre has the head of a pig.
15 In place of teeth, the ogre has rows of tiny grasping
hands.
16 One of the ogre’s arms is a tentacle.
17 The ogre has wattles.
18 Great, fluid-filled cysts bulge from the ogre’s skin.
19 The ogre has red-rimmed eyes where its nipples
should be.
20 From the waist down, the ogre’s body is that of an
enormous slug and it leaves a slimy trail wherever it
goes.
Variant Ogres
The trolls bred many kinds of ogres to serve various
functions in their wars against the faeries. Most of the
specialized breeds died out long ago, but a few remain
and are at large in the world today.
Boogeyman
Life on the edges of the civilized lands is anything
but easy. Between the ordinary troubles one might
face—wild animals, blights, droughts, storms, and
the like—people must also contend with strange and
malevolent creatures stalking the nights, bent on
mischief and worse. One breed of ogre that has grown
large in the nightmares of children all over are the
boogeymen. These brutes have developed a taste for
the succulent flesh of children and go to great lengths
to feed their unspeakable hunger.
Boogeymen stand about ten feet tall and have thick
muscular bodies with heavy abdomens that descend
to about their knees. They have the heads of red-
furred lions with copper-colored eyes. Despite their
bulky forms, they move with surprising stealth when
infiltrating homes to snatch their favored meals from
their beds.
BOOGEYMAN DIFFICULTY 50
Perception 12 (+2); Darksight
Defense 16, Health 60, Insanity —, Corruption 1d3 + 1
Strength 16 (+6), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 11 (+1)
Descriptor Ogre, Size 2, Speed 12
Languages Common Tongue, Trollish
Frightening A creature not immune to the Frightened
affliction makes attack rolls against the boogeyman with 1
bane.
Silent A boogeyman makes no sound when it moves unless it
chooses to.
Melee Attack—Teeth Strength (+6) with 1 boon (3d6)
Attack Roll 20+ If the boogeyman has no swallowed
creature inside its space, a Size 1 or smaller target moves
into the boogeyman’s space—the boogeyman unhinges its
jaw and swallows the target whole.
The target has the Blinded, Deafened, and Immobilized
afflictions while swallowed. It moves whenever the
boogeyman moves to remain in its space. At the end
of each round, the target takes 2d6 damage from the
boogeyman’s digestive juices. A swallowed target
can attack the boogeyman from inside its space. The
boogeyman’s gullet has Defense 10.
When the boogeyman’s damage total equals its Health
score, it vomits any creature it has swallowed along with
the remains of other creatures. All fall into a heap inside a
Size 2 space adjacent to the boogeyman’s space.
Stinking Mist The boogeyman can use an action to turn into
a cloud of stinking mist until the end of its turn. The cloud
fills its space with partial obscurement. While in this form,
the boogeyman ignores damage from all sources, moves
by flying, and can pass through spaces wide enough to
permit the passage of air as well as spaces occupied by
other creatures. Any breathing creature that enters the
boogeyman’s space makes a Will challenge roll. On a
failure, the creature becomes Diseased until the end of its
next turn.

---

Ettin
Ettins are ogres born with two heads and are common
enough that most people consider them a breed apart;
ettins who mate with other ettins or ogres, however,
always have ettin offspring. Ettins resemble ogres in
size and stature, and each head usually has its own
neck. There are some ettins who have two faces on
one overlarge, misshapen head, or have their second
head emerging from an unusual place in their bodies,
but these are few and far between.
With a second head comes a second personality,
and each head has its own distinct voice and manner
of speaking. Ettins are famous for bickering with
themselves, arguing over what to do or whom to
attack, often getting distracted enough to allow their
enemies to slip away. Conflicting desires can prevent
ettins from getting much done, but when they do
reach an accord, they pursue their goals with an
almost single-minded dedication.
ETTIN DIFFICULTY 100
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 15, Health 80, Insanity 1d3 + 1, Corruption 1d3 + 1
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 9 (–1)
Descriptor Ogre, Size 2, Speed 10
Languages Trollish
Immune Dazed, Stunned
Two Heads The ettin increases the number of actions and
triggered actions it can use in a round by 1. The ettin loses
access to this trait while injured.
Melee Attack—Flail Strength (+5) with 1 boon (3d6 + 2)
Devour The ettin can use an action to target one Size 1 or
smaller Defenseless or Unconscious creature in reach. It
picks up and eats the target, killing it instantly.
Vomit The ettin can use a triggered action when harmed to
spray semi-digested food from one if its mouth into a Size
3 space adjacent to its own space. Each object in the space
vulnerable to acids takes 2d6 damage. Each creature in the
space takes 1d6 damage and makes an Agility challenge
roll. On a failure, the creature takes 1d6 extra damage.
The ettin loses access to this trait until it uses Devour or
completes rest.

---

Horned Ogre
The trolls’ flirtation with the Void’s dark forces in the
practice of their magic stained both the world and the
foul creations the trolls made to live in it. Ogres and
giants walk in the Demon Lord’s shadow and thus
attract all kinds of demonic attention. This attention
transforms them, elevating them above their simple-
minded hunger to true cunning and pure evil. Among
the transformed can be found the horned ogres,
creatures who dwarf their kin both in terms of stature
and brutality.
Horned ogres dwell in places stained by the Void,
making their homes in ruined cities, crumbling
fortresses, or landscapes warped by the Demon
Lord’s fell influence. There, they attract other beings
enthralled by the Hunger in the Void to serve them,
from beastmen and cultists to monsters and other
abominations, all heaving and lurching from the
shadows to lend their might to whatever dread
purpose their dark lord demands. While horned ogres
might bow to more powerful masters, within their
own realms they rule as absolute tyrants over the
lesser creatures drawn there, obeying their masters in
a never-ending fear of being snatched up and eaten.
HORNED OGRE DIFFICULTY 250
Perception 11 (+1); Darksight
Defense 14, Health 120, Insanity —, Corruption 1d3 + 1

damage and then loses access to this trait for 24 hours

+ 6)

It picks up and eats the target, killing it instantly.

Oubliette Hammer
Some horned ogres carry hammers with a head
large enough to capture and contain a creature.
When the horned ogre has a Size 1 or smaller
creature Grabbed, the ogre can use an action to
stuff it inside the hammer. Make a Strength attack
roll against the target’s Strength. On a success,
the horned ogre locks the creature inside where it
remains until released. Any creature that can reach
the hammer while it’s not being held or carried
by the ogre can use an action to open the door.
A creature trapped inside the hammer’s head
cannot perceive beyond it and has total cover from
everything outside the hammer.
When the horned ogre makes an attack with its
hammer, the creature inside it takes 2d6 damage
and makes an Agility challenge roll. On a failure, the
creature takes 2d6 extra damage.
Oni
The forests of Balgrendia conceal many terrible
things, horrors most people in the comparatively
civilized north cannot conceive. For the average
Balgrendian, these monstrous threats are just another
part of living at the edge of civilization. The ogres of
Balgrendia, called oni by the locals, do not suffer from
the stupidity or slavish hunger of their lesser kin.
Rather, the oni are cunning and crafty, but thoroughly

---

debased and wicked, eagerly spreading misery,
disease, and other unpleasantness wherever they can.
Some believe the oni descend from the first ogres
created by the trolls, while other tales recount the acts
of ogres cunning enough to kill and eat the trolls who
created them, thus gaining their power.
Oni stand about ten feet tall and weigh upwards
of eight hundred pounds. They have exaggerated,
hideous features, with mouths stretched wide into
frightening grimaces under black, glassy eyes. They
have two great, smooth horns breaking from their
brows, extending another two feet from their heads.
Most display some strange mutation, with extra eyes
or digits being most common. Their skin tone also
runs the gamut, with most being color of midnight or
that of hot coals. They carry iron clubs and gird their
loins with animal skins.

Unlike other ogres, oni possess an assortment of
supernatural abilities that help them infiltrate their
victims’ communities. Some stalk their prey invisibly,
or alter their physical forms to resemble someone
they killed and ate to deceive and then feast upon the
other members of their victim’s families. The mere
presence of an oni in a community is dangerous to
everyone who lives there, for these brutes also spread
disease and misfortune wherever they linger.
Stallo
In stark contrast to the deadly cunning and
wickedness of the onis are the stallos. Gigantic ogres
of staggering stupidity, they haunt the frozen wastes
where they gorge themselves on seals, seabirds, and
the occasional traveler upon which they happen.
Stallos have nearly died out several times over the
centuries, but somehow a small population of them
endures across the wastes and into Blötland.
A typical stallo stands about 20 feet tall and weighs
several tons. It usually has bluish-white skin, with red-
rimmed eyes, and profuse body hair. It also has a great
sagging gut into which it stuffs whatever it can fit into
its cavernous maw.
Stallos know a few words of Trollish, but they prefer
to grunt instead of forming words.

Vodyanoy
On the edge of the wilderness, whenever a dam bursts
and floods farmlands, or a mill’s waterwheel breaks
and falls, or a strong swimmer inexplicably drowns,
people blame the vodyanoy, a creature believed to be
an evil water spirit or faerie that hates all living things
that dwell on the land. While these tales are correct
in portraying the vodyanoy as hateful and malevolent,
it is most definitely not a faerie. Rather, it is a rare
breed of ogre, perhaps cursed long ago by faerie
magic, condemned to live in the bogs, lakes, and rivers
scattered across the wilderness.
To look upon a vodyanoy is to know its evil. It
resembles a naked old man with long hair and a thick
green beard clumped with algae, slime, and pieces
of dead fish. It has the facial features of a frog, but
with red eyes that burn like hot coals. Although the
vodyanoy is an excellent swimmer, it prefers to float
about on a half-sunken log, its limbs dangling in the
water, sometimes lazily paddling, as it watches the
shores through slitted eyes for any sign of prey.
While the vodyanoy is smaller than a regular ogre
and far more intelligent, it shares the same driving
hunger of its land-dwelling kin. It likes nothing better
than to get its webbed paws on a nice fat child or
halfling—both succulent, and easier to subdue than
larger folk.
A vodyanoy doesn’t court trouble, but it can’t go too
long without eating—it will often work mischief upon
a nearby community to lure larger victims into its
clutches, or to cause enough confusion so it can slip
in and grab an unguarded child. The vodyanoy can
cast water-based spells, using its magic to harass and
drown its victims.
```

## 59. Guardians of the Cosmic Egg — Naga Technology

**Fonte:** *Guardians of The Cosmic Egg.pdf*  
**Cobertura:** PDF pp. 8–10. [EQUIPAMENTO] [DEPENDÊNCIA OMITIDA]

A aquisição de Naga Technology substitui descobertas de traditions/aprendizado de spells; esses blocos de magia continuam fora do escopo, mas a regra mínima de acesso é mantida porque é necessária para operar os dispositivos.

```text
Naga
Technology
Over the thousands of years since coming to Urth, the
nagas did their best to preserve the technology from their
ruined civilization. Each colony has several such items and,
though maintained and protected, few know how to use
them—their functions have become mysteries.
The nagas deemed these treasures too special to risk
their loss for some time, so they remain hidden away. But
with recent moves to connect with outsiders, some nagas
want to bring forth these items to help protect themselves
and to use in the struggle to save this world.
Using Naga
Technology
Whenever you discover a tradition, you can choose to
discover Naga Technology instead. Upon doing so, you gain
one device. Each time you would learn a spell, you can gain
another device in lieu of learning a spell from a different
tradition. The GM might restrict access to Naga Technology
to characters of this ancestry. Only a creature who has
discovered Naga Technology can make use of its devices.
If a device requires an action for activation prior to its use
in an attack or a challenge, consider the attack or challenge
to be part of the activation action.
Naga Devices
Below are some common items of Naga Technology that
you might expect to uncover in a typical community.
BENT TIME AMULET
A fist-sized, egg-shaped medallion hangs from a thick gold
chain. When activated, the egg flows into myriad bizarre
shapes before returning to its normal form.
Effect: Use an action, or a triggered action at any point in
the round, to activate this device. When you do so, you
gain one action that you must use immediately or lose.
The amulet has d3 charges. It replenishes its charges
24 hours after the expenditure of its last charge. When
it has replenished its charges, roll a d3 to see how many
charges it has.
CHERISHED STONE
Small enough to fit in the palm of one’s hand, this egg-
shaped stone features shifting, twisting swirls of color
across its surface.
Effect: Use an action to activate the stone, which causes it
to become ephemeral and swell in size. It grows until it
completely encompasses you, at which point it returns to
its normal hardness. The stone remains in this form for
1 hour per point of your Power score, until it’s destroyed
or until you use an action to end the effect. When it ends,
the stone returns to its normal form.

---

		 The Cherished Stone hovers 1 yard above a solid
surface. You can see out of the egg, but no one else can
see inside it. No effects originating from you can pass
through the egg, but the device produces breathable air
along with a warm, comfortable environment.
		 When you move, the Cherished Stone moves in a
direction you choose, up to a number of yards equal to
three times your Power score. The egg has a Defense
5 and Health equal to 10 × your Power score. If it is
destroyed, you fall prone under the space the stone
occupied, and the effect ends.
		 Once you activate the Cherished Stone, you must wait
24 hours before you can activate it again.
DEVASTATOR PISTOL
Its shape resembling a hand-held firearm makes the
Devastator Pistol’s function clear, though its activation
requires special training, as the weapon has no firing
mechanism. Instead, the wielder points the pistol at the
target and channels their will through the handle to release
a gray-green beam capable of making whatever it touches
disappear.
Effect: Use an action to activate the pistol. Target one
creature or object within medium range, then make
an Intellect attack roll against the target’s Agility. On a
success, the target takes 2d6 damage plus 1d6 damage
for each point of your Power score. If the damage
incapacitates or destroys the target, it vanishes along
with everything it wore and carried. On a failure, roll a d6;
on a 1, the weapon becomes nonfunctional for 24 hours.
		 The Devastator Pistol has 8 charges. It replenishes its
charges 24 hours after the expenditure of its last charge.
INSTANT TRANSPORT RING
On placing this silver band on one’s finger, metal spikes
extend into the flesh to hold it in place. Once worn, the ring
cannot be removed without cutting off the digit.
Effect: Use an action to activate the device. Target
one empty space you can see within long range. You
disappear in a riot of swirling colors that fade when you
reappear in the target space.
		 The Instant Transport Ring has 5 charges. It
replenishes its charges 24 hours after the expenditure of
its last charge.
MASK OF INFILTRATION
This smooth, featureless mask of porcelain fits snugly over
the face. Once you place it there, it remains until you use
an action to remove it or until you become incapacitated.
Although the mask covers your face completely, you can
see, smell, and breathe normally.
Effect: Use an action to activate this device. You transform
into a flesh-and-blood creature with a humanoid shape
of your choice, such as human, dwarf, or molekin. You
make all decisions about the appearance of the form
you chose. You use your normal rules, regardless of your
appearance. You retain this appearance until you remove
the mask or become incapacitated.
		 The Mask of Infiltration has 3 charges. It replenishes its
charges 24 hours after the expenditure of its last charge.

---

SHOCK LANCE
The tip of this 2-yard-long tapering metal shaft throws
sparks when activated. The weapon features two rubber
grips.
Effect: Activating the Shock Lance counts as a minor
activity. Once activated, it remains so for 1 minute. The
Shock Lance uses the rules for a spear. When activated,
your attacks with it deal an extra 1d6 damage per point
of your Power score. In addition, when you deal damage
to a flesh-and-blood target, the target becomes impaired
until the end of your next turn.
		 Once you activate the Shock Lance, you must wait 1
hour before you can activate it again.
SONIC SCRAMBLER
The Sonic Scrambler fits in the palm of one’s hand and has
a rectangular shape, with a convex depression on one side.
Effect: Use an action to activate this device. The Sonic
Scrambler emits a field that extends away from it in a
5-yard radius for a number of rounds equal to 1 + your
Power score. All creatures in the field, other than you,
become deafened. At the end of each round, sound
waves travel from the device to brutalize everything in
the area except you. Each flesh-and-blood creature and
object in the area takes 1d6 damage, 2d6 damage if your
Power is 3 or higher, or 3d6 damage if your Power is 5
or higher. A creature in the field can make a Strength
challenge roll. On a success, the creature takes no
damage.
		 Once you activate the Sonic Scrambler, you must wait
1 hour before you can activate it again.
VOID ROD
This black rod, 24 inches long and 2 inches thick, has a
concave depression a third of the way up one side.
Effect: Use an action to activate this device. When you do
so, make an Intellect challenge roll with 2 banes. On a
success, you target one empty space within medium
range and open a hole to the Void in that space. The
hole remains open for a number of rounds equal to 1 +
your Power score. Any creature that starts its turn within
short range of the target space becomes slowed until the
start of its next turn and makes a Will challenge roll. On a
failure, the creature senses something awful in the Void
and gains 1 Insanity.
		 At the end of each round, roll a d6. If you roll a 6,
a small demon emerges from the hole. You gain 1
Corruption. The demon treats all creatures that are not
demons as enemies and takes the next available turn to
attack.
		 If you get a failure, nothing happens unless the result
of the roll is 0 or less. If this occurs, chaotic energy
explodes from the device to deal 6d6 damage to you
and everything else within short range of it. A creature
in range can make an Agility challenge roll; on a success,
the creature takes just half the damage.
		 If you attempt to activate this device in the Void, it has
no effect. Once you use the Void Rod, you must wait 24
hours before you can use it again.
WARDICLE
A robe of many different colors, the Wardicle adjusts its
size to accommodate the wearer. Once activated, the colors
shimmer and writhe.
Effect: Use an action to activate this device. For 1 minute,
you remain protected from magic. You take half damage
from all magical effects. When a creature uses magic to
attack you, you impose 1 bane on the attack roll. When
you would make a challenge roll to mitigate a magical
effect, you roll with 1 boon.
		 While under the effects of the Wardicle, you can use an
action to end the effect early and make attack rolls and
challenge rolls with 2 boons until the end of your next
turn.
		 The Wardicle has 3 charges. It replenishes its charges
24 hours after the expenditure of its last charge.
WARRIOR’S BREASTPLATE
The Warrior’s Breastplate displays intricate and detailed
engravings that show naga warriors battling demons. The
breastplate adjusts its size to accommodate its wearer.
Anyone wearing it has Defense equal to their Agility + 4.
Effect: Use an action, or a triggered action at any time
during the round, to activate the device. Once activated,
the breastplate emits a green field that completely
envelops you for a number of rounds equal to 1 + your
Power score. While it remains active, you take no damage
from attacks made using ordinary ranged weapons, and
you impose 1 bane on attack rolls made against you
using ordinary melee weapons.
		 The Warrior’s Breastplate has 3 charges. It replenishes
its charges 24 hours after the expenditure of its last
charge.
```

## 61. Of Gears and Ghosts — August Talismans, Sickstone & Gray Wasting

**Fonte:** *Of Gears and Ghosts.pdf*  
**Cobertura:** PDF pp. 2–3. [EQUIPAMENTO] [REGRA]

**August Talismans (p. 2).** A referência nominal a *bind soul to machine* é mantida sem reproduzir a spell.

```text
August Talismans
These intricate clockwork-and-jade vests lie at the
heart of the Guild’s prodigious ability to produce
clockworks using the bind soul to machine spell.
The Black Books, knowing that the most skilled
and powerful among the Guild inevitably fell to
madness and corruption, devised the first of these
strange protections in the sixth century. Worn
by those summoning forth the souls needed to
power a creation, each August Talisman can absorb
1d3 Corruption (for lesser August Talismans) or
1d6 Corruption (for greater August Talismans).
Using a Talisman is not without danger—for
every point of Corruption it absorbs, its wearer
must make a Will challenge roll with a number of
banes equal to the total Corruption the Talisman
currently contains. Success means the Talisman
functions normally. Failure results in the Talisman
immediately becoming sickstone, inflicting half of
the Corruption it contains on the wearer.
```

**Sickstone, exposição e Gray Wasting (p. 3).**

```text
Sickstone
The corrupted, foul byproduct of August
Talismans, sickstone has the appearance of
soot-stained, luminescent jade whose nauseating
radiance penetrates all but the thickest walls. The
light it gives off is of no color known to Urth, but
it burns the flesh and scars the soul regardless. It
is corruption incarnate and poses incredible risk
to any who come near it.
Sickstone exposure is measured in terms of
intensity and time. Low intensity is unshielded
exposure to a small amount (an ounce or less)
of sickstone at short range. Moderate intensity
extends the unshielded range to medium for
amounts of up to a pound. High intensity requires
amounts of sickstone up to 2 pounds and has
a range of long. Amounts exceeding 2 pounds
are considered severe intensity at long range.
Shielding oneself from exposure requires 4 yards
of stone or earth, 1 yard of water, or 1 inch of
lead or quicksilver per degree of intensity. The
protective field spell fulfills the requirement as
well, nullifying the sickstone’s intensity for the
spell’s duration.
Sickstone Exposure
Intensity* 1 Round 1 Minute 1 Hour 1 Day
Low — Stage 0 Stage 1 Stage 2
Moderate Stage 0 Stage 1 Stage 2 Stage 3
High Stage 1 Stage 2 Stage 3 Stage 4
Severe Stage 2 Stage 3 Stage 4 Stage 4
*Direct physical contact with sickstone increases the degree
of intensity by one step.
Gray Wasting
Gray wasting afflicts living mortal creatures exposed to
sickstone. An afflicted creature develops burns on and in
its body that blister and break until the creature dies. The
sickness is insidious and can be carried by constructs,
faeries, demons, and the undead, even though they do not
suffer from its effects.
Exposure Any creature exposed to sickstone is at risk
of suffering gray wasting. In addition, a living mortal
creature exposed to sickstone might expose other
creatures. An exposed creature counts as being
contaminated with low intensity if it suffered moderate
exposure, moderate intensity if it suffered high exposure,
and high intensity if it suffered severe exposure. The
intensity drops by one step each time the exposed
creature completes a rest.
Transmission A living creature exposed to sickstone must
make a Strength challenge roll when it next completes
a rest. The creature makes this roll with a number of
banes determined by its degree of exposure: 1 (low),
2 (moderate), 3 (high), or 4 (severe). On a failure, the
creature suffers the stage 1 effects of gray wasting.
Cure Gray wasting counts as a disease and is treated as such.
Stage 0 Reduce the creature’s degree of exposure by one
step. If this would reduce the exposure below low, the
creature recovers from gray wasting and removes the
penalty to Health.
Stage 1 The creature takes a cumulative –1d6 penalty to
Health and gains 1 Corruption.
Stage 2 The creature takes a cumulative –1d6 penalty to
Health and gains a Mark of Darkness regardless of its
Corruption score. While at this stage, the creature is also
impaired.
Stage 3 The creature takes a cumulative –1d6 penalty to
Health, and gains 1 Insanity and 1 Corruption. It gains
a second Mark of Darkness. While at this stage, the
creature is also impaired and slowed.
Stage 4 The creature dies and its contaminated flesh
becomes a monster of its Size.
Recovery Each time a creature suffering gray wasting
completes a rest, it must make a Strength challenge roll
with a number of banes based on its current degree of
exposure (see Transmission).
• 20 or more: The disease moves down one stage.
• Success: No change.
• Failure: The disease moves up one stage.
• 0 or less: The disease moves up two stages.
```

## 63. Paths of Iron — special materials & Clockwork Attachments

**Fonte:** *Paths of Iron.pdf*  
**Cobertura:** PDF pp. 2–4. [EQUIPAMENTO]

**Heavy Metals (pp. 2–3).** Inclui Alchemical Glass, Dark Steel, Dragonbone e Blood Iron, com preços multiplicadores e efeitos especiais.

```text
Heavy Metals
Nearly all civilizations that have risen and fallen in
the lands of Rûl have followed the same progression
of materials for manufacturing tools and weapons.
Exploration of old ruins turned up tools and weapons
made of stone, wood, and, sometimes, bone, all
serviceable for hunting, striping bark from trees, and
digging, but new tools developed as people found
metal that littered the ground or they found it in their
digging. Copper and brass gave way to bronze, which
fades with the discovery of iron. Experimentation
with smelting metals and advanced forging
techniques leads to the production of steel.
Iron, steel, and bronze remain the most common
throughout the lands, but alchemists, engineers,
and others have experimented with the existing
techniques and incorporating other materials for the
manufacture of weapons and tools that prove superior
even to folded steel.
Alchemical Glass
With the understanding that alchemists work with
volatile materials, it ought to surprise no one that one
of the first achievements of their ancient, secret order
was the introduction of a material capable of holding
the substances they must regularly use. Nearly all
alchemical glass objects take the form of small bottles
for holding priceless powders and liquids. The glass
has a greenish hue and can withstand jostling against
other objects, survive falls, and resist great pressure
without cracking or chipping.
Only in recent times have the alchemical glass
blowers experimented with fashioning arms from
the substance and, despite the many doubts about its
serviceability, alchemical glass weapons take an edge
that is not only sharper than metal, but holds its edge
better too.
Price: Any edged or pointed weapon can be made
from alchemical glass, though few have spread
outside Lij, and sell for 50 times the normal price.
Keenest Edge: When you attack a creature of flesh
and blood with an alchemical glass weapon and the
total of your attack roll is 20 or higher and beats the
target number by at least 5, the target of the attack
takes an extra 2d6 damage and becomes impaired
until the end of your next turn.
Dark Steel
Some thirty years ago, an expedition into the
Desolation recovered two swords, a dagger, and a
shoulder-guard from one of the Black Pyramids rising
up from the blood-red sands. The material from
which the objects were made aroused interest for they
were made from something unknown, something the
discoverers called dark steel. The weapons could have
been newly forged, as they showed no signs of use,
no scratches in the matte black surfaces. The metal
had some flexibility, but the sword snapped back to its
original straightness after being bent nearly in half.
No amount of polishing put a gloss on the surface
and no abrasive short of diamonds could scratch their
surfaces.
Price: Since its discovery, searchers have uncovered
more dark steel items, enough to make them
expensive curiosities instead of pricy artifacts. Metal
armor and weapons made from dark steel sell for 100
times their normal list price.
Essence of Darkness: Dark steel items diminish
light in their midst, halving the range of light
produced by light sources within medium range of it.
Faerie Bane: When it comes to affecting faeries,
iron is to dark steel what a candle’s flame is to a
bonfire. All faeries within short range of a dark steel
weapon or armor become impaired for as long as they
remain within this range. In addition, any faerie that
takes damage from a dark steel weapon must succeed
on a Strength challenge roll or become fatigued
for 1 minute or take an extra 1d6 damage if already
fatigued.
Dragonbone
Long ago, before the Hateful Wars between the faeries
and the trolls, dragons controlled the lands. Some
carved out nations for themselves, enslaving the
lesser immortal peoples to serve their needs, while
others were simply forces of ruin, killing everything
that drew near. Some calamity toppled the dragons
from their high perch, and allowed their servants to
rise up and choose their own destiny. Of the dragons,
their bodies rotted until only their bones remained,
and dragon bones never break down, never splinter or
break, and retain their density regardless of their age.
Dragonbone would become the favored material
for weapons shaped and enchanted by both trolls and
faeries alike. As a result, the weapons that have survived
through the centuries bear potent magical properties
that make them unique and priceless arms. The elves
have never forgotten how to work with dragonbone and
some artisans have begun working with the materials
to arm the faeries against the encroaching darkness.
Price: Dragonbone can be shaped into any kind
of weapon or ammunition, but it’s not normally
available for sale. Instead, one might receive a
dragonbone weapon as a gift or steal one from the
faeries. Dragonbone weapons can go for 500 times
their normal price or more.

---

Moaning: Weapons made from dragonbone might
moan when used in combat. When you attack with
a dragonbone weapon and the total of your attack
roll is 20 or higher and beats the target number by
at least 5, the voice of the dead dragon emerges from
the weapon as a moan for 1 minute. Any creature
other than you that hears the moaning must get a
success on a Will challenge roll or gain 1 Insanity.
Breath of the Dragon: Whenever you attack with
a weapon made from dragonbone and you roll a
17 or higher on the die, the target of your attack
must get a success on an Agility challenge roll with
1 bane or catch fire, taking 1d6 damage at the end of
each round until a creature uses an action to douse
the flames.
Blood Iron
The Endless Steppe burns and the smoke from
the wildfires now stains the western horizon.
Nomadic halflings have carried news of strange
invaders having made landfall, seemingly intent on
conquest. The invaders have made a slaughter of
the few centaur tribes to engage them, but now a
Great Khan has appeared among the Zephyr Clan
attempting to unite the tribes to drive the invaders
back into the sea.
Of this new threat, there are reports of them being
humans of enormous size, big, hulking, rivaling the
jotun of the far south, but with scarlet skin and black
hair, bodies marked with brands and tattoos where
not covered by the shaggy fur of animal hides they
wear. More noteworthy than their appearance is
their weaponry, for the warriors wield blades of red
metal whose merest touch can cause the living to
sicken and die. The blood iron, as it has come to be
known, is translucent, so that it looks as if the blades
were cut rubies or made from cinnabar.
Price: Few blood iron weapons made their way
across the Shield Mountains and the ones that
have were brought out from the growing conflict by
opportunistic sellswords and treasure hunters who
have seized the opportunity to explore the Endless
Steppe. As a result, prices for these exceedingly rare
weapons hover around 200 times the normal price.
Toxic Metal: Any creature of flesh and blood
injured by an attack made using a weapon forged
from blood iron becomes poisoned. At the end of
each round, a creature poisoned in this way takes
1d6 damage unless it gets a success on a Strength
challenge roll with 1 bane. Three successes from
challenge rolls made to resist the poison removes the
poisoned affliction from the target.
```

**Clockwork Attachments (pp. 3–4).** Embora sejam instalados em personagens clockwork, são equipamentos com preço/disponibilidade próprios; Body Composition e backgrounds de ancestry foram omitidos.

```text
Clockwork
Attachments
You can upgrade your body by using attachments.
Clockwork Attachments
Attachment Price Availability
Coiled springs 1 gc Uncommon
Impact absorbers 1 gc Rare
Internal transceiver 15 gc Exotic
Passenger compartment 10 gc Rare
Retractable blades 2 gc Uncommon
Coiled Springs: A clockwork fitted with these
springs can jump three times its normal distance.
Once used in this way, the clockwork must spend 1
minute concentrating to reset the mechanism.
Impact Absorbers: With shocks and impact
absorbers installed, the clockwork takes half damage
from falling. If the clockwork would take 20 damage
or more from landing after a fall, the absorbers break
and must be replaced before they can be used again.
Internal Transceiver: A clockwork with an
internal transceiver can communicate with any other
clockwork that also has an internal transceiver, as
long as they are within 1 mile of each other.
Passenger Compartment: The clockwork’s interior
contains space enough to hold one creature of a size
smaller than it. While inside this space, the creature
cannot see or hear anything that happens outside
it, cannot be targeted by attacks or other effects, and
has enough air to breathe for 8 hours. A creature
must use an action to enter or exit this space. If the
clockwork with the compartment becomes injured,
the creature it carries in its space, must succeed on a
Strength challenge roll or take half the damage that
injured the clockwork. If the clockwork becomes
incapacitated or destroyed, the creature it carries
takes the damage that incapacitated or destroyed the
clockwork and falls prone in the empty space nearest
to the clockwork.
Retractable Blades: Once installed into the hands,
the clockwork can use a triggered action on its turn
to extend or retract the blades. While extended, the
blades count as swift weapons that deal 1d6 damage
and have the finesse property. Retracted blades are
fully hidden inside the clockwork’s body.
```

```text
Blooded Warrior
Anyone swearing the sacred oaths of loyalty to the Horned
King becomes a blooded warrior. Each bears their god’s
mark on their brows: a bloody smudge that stays no matter
how often they wash—not that they wash all that much.
Blooded warriors have no doubts about their purpose and
give their lives to further the cult’s cause.
BLOODED WARRIOR DIFFICULTY 5
Perception 9 (–1)

Horned Priest
Priests of the Horned King started the Wild Beasts cult and
control it still. Although many of the god’s priests disagree
with their message and find their actions reprehensible, the
horned priests command divine magic, which tells all that
they act with their master’s blessing.
Horned priests typically wear leather breechclouts and
furred cloaks. They cover their bodies with mud and work
it into their hair to keep insects at bay. While the mud is
still wet, they use their fingers to draw their god’s symbol on
their chests: a horned bull’s head.

priest can howl at the start of their turn to produce either
of the following effects.
• Each friendly creature within medium range and that
lacks the deafened affliction can either end the dazed
and frightened conditions or use a triggered action to
attack.
• Each hostile creature within medium range and that
lacks the deafened affliction makes a Will challenge
roll with 1 bane. On a failure, the creature becomes
frightened for 1 minute. The affliction ends early if the
affected creature deals damage on its turn.
Once the horned priest uses this trait, they lose access to it
for 1 minute.

With Claws and Teeth The horned priest uses an action,
or a triggered action on their turn, to target one friendly
creature within short range. The target gains a wolf’s fur
and fangs for 1 minute. Until this effect ends, the target’s
melee attacks deal 1d6 extra damage.
```

```text
Horned Champion
Every warrior who becomes a horned champion undergoes
the Rite of Becoming. The candidate strips off all clothing,
dons a blindfold, and then marches off into the deepest
woods. At some point later, the Horned King finds them. If
he deems them worthy, the god has his way with them. If
not, they never return. Bloodied, bruised, weakened, and
filled to the brim with divine seed, they transform to adopt
their god’s likeness.
All horned champions have sharp antlers growing from
their foreheads, eyes that shine with green light, and whorls
in their skin. They say nothing as the god fills their minds
with strange visions of being wild animals hunting prey in
the woods. All distraction falls away in battle, though. They
fight with singular focus to kill their opponents.
```

**A Wild Beasts Campaign — Shadow of the Demon Lord effects (pp. 4–5).** Os benefícios de adesão e paths de personagem que começam em *The Wild’s Call* foram excluídos.

```text
A Wild Beasts
Campaign
Their single-minded purpose and their zeal in carrying
out their mission make the Wild Beasts a singular threat to
the stability of the Northern Reach. Unlike the beastmen
horde, Wild Beasts have sufficient intelligence to outwit
defenders and the resolve to keep fighting, even after
suffering disastrous setbacks. Their warped interpretation
of the Horned King risks transforming the god into
something monstrous and evil.
The following entries provide you with a broad-strokes
story so you can create adventures that feature the cult
as the primary antagonist. In addition, each tier includes
a Shadow of the Demon Lord entry to show how the
corruption burgeons to make it easier for the Hunger in the
Void to enter this world and consume it.
The Gathering Beasts
(Novice)
One by one, villages and hamlets all across the western
hinterlands go dark as the Wild Beasts invade. The
barbarians punch through walls, chop up the defenders,
and take as prisoners the rest. Captured people can join the
Wild Beasts. Any potential convert must demonstrate their
worth and faith by killing one of their neighbors. The rest
end up marched east or butchered.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: All natural and ordinary
animals become aggressive. Even domesticated animals
turn on their keepers. Cattle stampede to trample
handlers, while horses buck off riders and kick them
while they’re down. Pets run off, some even attacking
their owners before vanishing.

---

Horned Prince (Expert)
One of the horned champions declares himself the true son
of the Horned King, the god clad in mortal flesh. Dubbed
the Horned Prince, he takes control over the cult by killing
several priests, specifically those who doubt his divinity.
The survivors fall into line and the host’s numbers swell
with beastmen welcomed into their ranks. The Wild Beasts,
emboldened by their new leader, push into settled lands.
A force camps around Crossings to lay siege, while the rest
spread through the surrounding lands. The Wild Beasts no
longer take prisoners; they kill everyone.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: Ordinary people’s patience
and tolerance drain out of them until they become bitter
and angry. Friendships fail, families break apart, violent
crime erupts just about everywhere. People who give
in to their aggressive tendencies discover patches of fur
sprouting from their bodies, and their facial features
become bestial.
A Monstrous God (Master)
The Wild Beasts overrun the Northern Reach, from the
Firepeaks to the shores of the Auroral Ocean. They have
become a horde comprising human and monstrous
members. The host pours through the Shadow Pass
enabling travel to the south and invades the Empire,
already vulnerable from its own internecine struggles.
As mighty as the horde has become, though, it shows
weakness. Warriors removed from the Horned Prince lose
some of their aggressiveness and can be easily confused.
Killing the Horned Prince might cause the whole host to
fall apart.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: People everywhere start
transforming into beastmen of all kinds. The change
happens without warning and takes just a few
excruciating minutes. The new beastmen turn on their
friends and family, killing anyone who has not yet
transformed. The effect extends for about 100 miles
from the Horned Prince.
```

- **Disciple of The Demon Lord.pdf** — conteúdo mecânico é o expert path Disciple of the Demon Lord, seus aspects e talentos.
- **In Plain Sight.pdf** — conteúdo mecânico relevante é a ancestry Ferren, equipamento inicial e paths.
- **Only Human.pdf** — conteúdo mecânico relevante expande a ancestry Human, tabelas de personagem e equipamento inicial.
- **Path of the Adept.pdf** — conteúdo mecânico é o novice path Adept e os talentos de Sources of Power.
- **Paths of Conflict.pdf** — conteúdo mecânico é composto por expert paths e seus talentos.
- **Paths of Darkness.pdf** — conteúdo mecânico é composto por master paths e seus talentos.
- **Paths of Science.pdf** — roguery talents e expert paths científicos; substâncias/criações aparecem como benefícios exclusivos dessas progressões.
- **The Scientific Method.pdf** — o Scientist novice path e as Sciences/gadgets são benefícios exclusivos do path, portanto não entram como regras/equipamentos autônomos.
- **Scions of Nature.pdf** — conteúdo mecânico relevante é a ancestry Hamadryad, equipamento inicial e master paths/forms de path.

## 68. Paragons of Virtue — Eudaemonic Bonds

**Fonte:** *Paragons of Virtue.pdf*  
**Cobertura:** PDF pp. 2–3. [REGRA] [DEPENDÊNCIA OMITIDA]

Os talentos concedidos em função do novice path foram deliberadamente cortados; permanecem apenas as regras comuns do vínculo e os Gifts/Weights de cada virtude.

```text
Eudaemonic Bonds
Anyone who displays the proper commitment to one of the
cardinal virtues might gain attention from an eudaemon,
but they offer no explanation for why they might single out
some but not others. One person could choose the good
instead of the tempting wrong and feel the eudaemon come
upon them, but another who delivers justice to a villain of
the highest order feels little more than the accomplishment
of a job well done.
Your character, however, stands apart from others of
your kind. Destiny steers your course, or you have a special
talent, or you just have a bit more luck than other folks
have. Provided you meet the requirements listed under the
eudaemons described below, you can apply the benefits
to your character. Note, though, that binding with a
eudaemon comes with some risk. The eudaemons aid those
who embody their virtues, but if their chosen fall short, the
eudaemons deliver swift and terrible punishment.
If you bond with an eudaemon, you will never be alone
again. You feel the entity around you—watching, weighing
your actions, judging you. The eudaemon has no body and
makes no sound, but you know they are always present.
Seeing symbols of the virtue the eudaemon represents
could reflect the actions of the entity, or it might just be
your mind playing tricks, showing you what you expect
to see. If ever you disappoint your eudaemon, you feel
their wrath coursing through your body. Unless you make
amends, you might lose them forever.

2

Bond Benefits
When you make the bond with the eudaemon, you gain
the following benefit and drawback. At level 4, you gain
the benefits associated with the eudaemon with which you
share a bond.
Eudaemon’s Favor: When you become incapacitated, you
can make an additional fate roll and choose the desired
result.
Hated Corruption: When you gain Corruption, you take
1d6 damage for each point of Corruption you have after
increasing your total.

Prudence
The eudaemon of Prudence embodies the virtue of good
decision-making and combines the elements of memory,
intelligence, and anticipation. Prudence appears as a
dragon, an owl, a human with three faces: wolf, lion, and
dog, a woman carrying a serpent and mirror, a compass, or
an open book.

LEVEL 4
Gift of Prudence: When you would make an Intellect attack roll
or challenge roll, you can, before you roll the dice, use this
trait to make the roll with 2 boons. Once you use this trait, you
lose access to it until you complete a rest.
Weight of Folly: Each time you gain 1 Corruption or more,
you gain 1d6 Insanity and, for a number of rounds equal to
your Insanity total, you choose targets at random from those
eligible, and you become hostile to all creatures.

---

Temperance

LEVEL 4
Gift of Temperance: You can use this trait when a creature you
can see would make an attack roll against your Intellect or Will
to impose 1 bane on the attack roll or when you would make
an Intellect or Will challenge roll to make the roll with 1 boon.
Then, you lose access to this trait until you complete a rest.
Weight of Excess: Each time you gain 1 Corruption or more, you
gain 1d6 Insanity and, for a number of rounds equal to your
Insanity total, you fall prone and cannot stand up.

---

Courage
Having the resolve to do what’s right regardless of the
consequences stands at the heart of the virtue of Courage.
People favored by Courage never back down or flinch when
in pursuit of good ends. Depictions of Courage include the
lion, phoenix, and sword.

LEVEL 4
Gift of Courage: If, at the end of the round, you are charmed or
frightened, you can make a Will challenge roll. On a success,
the affliction ends. You can use this trait three times. You
lose access to the trait after you expend the last use until you
complete a rest.
Weight of Cowardice: Each time you gain 1 Corruption or more,
you gain 1d6 Insanity and become impaired for a number of
rounds equal to your Insanity total.

---

Justice
The virtue of Justice requires one to walk between excess
and want and travel along the middle path without ever
straying. Living in balance helps one attain wisdom and
happiness. People touched by Justice also feel compelled to
right obvious wrongs, ensure that those in need receive the
aid they require, and take from those who exploit or harm
others through their greed, selfishness, and wickedness.
Common symbols of Justice include the scales and the
flame of truth.

LEVEL 4
Gift of Justice: If you or one of your allies within medium range
takes damage, gains an affliction, or is otherwise harmed, you
gain a +2 bonus to Speed and make attack rolls with 2 boons
until the end of your next turn. You can use this trait three
time. You lose access to the trait after you expend the last use
until you comlete a rest.
Weight of Injustice: Each time you gain 1 Corruption or more,
you gain 1d6 Insanity and become dazed for a number of
rounds equal to your Insanity total.
```


## 69. Unwelcome Guests — parasitas, curas e criaturas

**Fonte:** *Unwelcome Guests.pdf*  
**Cobertura:** PDF pp. 2–4. [REGRA] [EQUIPAMENTO] [CRIATURA]

A seção preserva o procedimento de progressão por estágios, curas e todos os blocos reutilizáveis do suplemento.

```text
Parasites

The parasites found below use the same format and
mechanical concepts as the diseases introduced in
Fever Dreams. A parasite’s entry tells you something
about it, how one becomes a host, the symptoms
of infection, and any known cures. The mechanics
follow.
Once a creature becomes infected with a parasite,
the infestation marks its progression through a
series of worsening stages that culminate in some
permanent impairment or death. At specific intervals
described in the recovery section, the afflicted
creature makes challenge rolls to resist the parasites.
The result of the roll causes the infection’s effect to
move up to a higher stage or down to a lower stage.
This continues until the infection reaches its final
stage or the creature becomes cured through a series
of successful rolls or from acquiring the actual cure.

Black Moth Larvae

“Black” fails to capture just how dark are the wings
of the black moths. These tiny insects seem to drink
in the light, and look like fluttering holes in reality.
Although small, delicate, fragile even, the black
moths pose terrible danger to other creatures and
infestations have been known to wipe out entire
communities.
Black moths lay their eggs in the bodies of living
creatures, typically when such creatures are asleep,
choosing places with access to the warm interior of
the body such as the nostrils, ear canals, or open
mouth. A moth can lay dozens of eggs, attaching
each to the walls with an adhesive made from its
reproductive juices, and then flutters off to die. Several
days later, the moth eggs hatch and the larvae eat
their way free from the host.
Purge Broth Finding and manually removing
the eggs inside a host’s body before they hatch
proves a fruitless exercise; the eggs are simply too
small and hide in places normally out of reach.
Apothecaries, especially those in rural areas, have
concocted a cure called purge broth, though people
who sample its foul flavor report the cure is as bad as
the infestation. Made from rotting stinkweed leaves,
powdered gallstones, and a number of other unsavory
substances (1 ss worth of exotic materials), the potion
must be consumed in a single swallow for maximum
effectiveness. The drinker experiences a strange
flushing, almost as if it was burning from inside
out. This flushing causes the larvae to exit the body
through the fastest available route, which causes the
drinker to take 1d6 + 3 damage as wriggling maggotlike things spill out in a bloody wash from all of its
orifices.

Black Moth Larvae Effects
Infection If a creature completes a rest in an outdoor
wilderness environment in an area containing at least
one black moth, the creature must, 1d3 + 1 days later,
make a Strength challenge roll with 1 bane. On a failure,
the creature suffers the effects of stage 1 infection.
While infected, the creature is diseased and, each time
it completes a rest, must make a Strength challenge roll
with an additional 1 bane, plus any banes imposed by the
stage. Find the results of the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from the black moth larvae
infection and becomes immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature has a 1d6 penalty to its Health and
makes Strength attack rolls and challenge rolls with 1
bane.
Stage 2 The creature has a 2d6 penalty to its Health and
makes Strength attack rolls and challenge rolls with 2
banes.
Stage 3 The creature has a 3d6 penalty to its Health and
makes Strength attack rolls and challenge rolls with 3
banes.
Stage 4 The creature takes damage equal to its Health
and releases from its body a cloud of black moths that
partially obscure the air within short range of the dead
creature for 1d6 rounds before dispersing.
Aftereffects The creature makes Strength attack rolls and
challenge rolls with 1 bane for 1d6 days.

Bloat Worms
Many parasites invade hosts through the food
they eat. Meat, in particular, can carry all kinds of
terrifying parasites, if it’s not properly cooked. Bloat
worms are one such parasite that breeds in spoiled
meat, though how they come to be there is anyone’s
guess. Creatures who consume the rancid flesh take in
the worms, which then spread throughout the host’s
body with alarming speed and to awful effect.
Bloat worms release gas as they feed on their hosts,
creating slowly expanding bubbles that eventually
push out the skin to form hardened bulges. A minor
infection might result in a few weirdly discolored
raised areas on the body, while the more severe
infections can make the hosts unrecognizable
monsters. If the host dies, the pent-up gas releases
with explosive force to blow apart the body in a
shower of blood, bones, and flapping skin.
Alcohol Binge The best way to rid oneself of bloat
worms is to drink several gallons of alcohol over a
period of seven days.
The change in blood
chemistry makes the
body inhospitable to
the bloat worms and,
at the end of the seventh
day, they evacuate in
a forceful spray from
the host’s bowels (as
the hateful defecation
Forbidden spell).

--- PDF p. 3 ---
Bloat Worm Effects
Infection When a creature consumes food contaminated
with bloat worms, it must, 8 hours later, make a Strength
challenge roll with 2 banes. On a failure, the creature
suffers the stage 1 infection. While infected, each time
the creature completes a rest, it must make another
Strength challenge roll with an additional 2 banes. Find
the results of the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from the bloat worms and
becomes immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature is diseased. While diseased in
this way, the creature makes rolls related to social
interactions with 1 bane.
Stage 2 As stage 1, but the creature is also impaired and
slowed. If the creature becomes incapacitated, it dies
and explodes, showering everything within short range
of it with gore.
Stage 3 As stage 2, but the creature takes 1d6 extra
damage whenever it takes damage.
Aftereffects The creature has a number of unseemly bulges
and growths from the bloat worms.

Intellect Eater

The dreaded intellect eater has been a scourge in
recent days and victims of these parasites have been
turning up in the Confederacy’s lands, especially in
the client villages and towns who support the larger
cities. Intellect eaters infest sewers and enter their
victims’ bodies through the openings of their sexual
organs and conceal their entry with the anesthetizing
slime their thin bodies exude.
Once inside the host, the eater coils around its
victim’s spine, where it remains dormant for a full year,
feeding on the host’s spinal fluid, while it grows ever
larger. When it reaches adulthood, the worm chews a
hole out from the base of its host’s throat. Fully sentient,
when the intellect eater partly emerges from the host, it
takes control of the host’s body and can communicate
using the host’s mouth and vocal cords.

Intellect Eater Effects
Infection A creature that moves through a fluid infested
with intellect eaters, such as in a pit underneath an
outhouse or a city sewer might become infected by
the parasite. Roll a d6. On a 6, the parasite invades the
host’s body by way of its genitals. While infected, the
host creature makes Agility attack rolls and challenge
rolls with 1 bane and grants 1 boon on attack rolls made
against its Agility. One year after infection, the worm
reaches maturity with the following effects.
A mature intellect eater shares control of the host
body until the host body dies, which kills the parasite as
well. The eater uses the following statistics.

INTELLECT EATER

DIFFICULTY 5

Size 1/8 horrifying monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense *; Health *; Insanity 0; Corruption 4
Strength 5 (–5), Agility 5 (–5), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 2
Shared Defense and Health The intellect eater uses the
host’s Defense and Health scores. The intellect eater can
also use the host’s Strength and Agility in place of its
own for as long as it resides in the host’s body.

Immune dazed, stunned
Parasite The intellect eater resides inside of its host’s body.
If the host dies, so too does the intellect eater. The eater
can use an action once per round, taking its turn when
its host does. The parasite uses its host’s body to resolve
the use of its action.

Mind Fire
It takes just one of these amorphous microorganisms
entering the body for it to wreak havoc. The
organism moves through its host along its blood
stream until it takes root in the brain, where it
remains, eating away at the gray matter until it is so
full of holes the victim dies. The infection causes
derangement, erratic behavior, and violent outbursts.
Victims of mind fire run a low fever and blood pools
in the sclera of their eyes.
Surgery The organism grows larger as it feeds on
its victim’s brain and its wet, slippery, formless body
fills in the holes that it creates. A victim at Stage 3
or higher might be rescued from the disease as the
parasite is of a size large enough to be surgically
extracted. A healer or surgeon can make the attempt,
which requires sawing away a portion of the skull
and rooting around inside the brain to reveal the
creature from the brain tissue its body has replaced.
Then, it’s just a matter of tongs and a firm grip to
remove it.
A creature who undergoes this surgery takes a
permanent 1d3 penalty to its Intellect score and
gains 1d6 Insanity, which cannot be reduced by
any means.

Mind Fire Effects
Infection The next time a creature who consumes
contaminated water or food completes a rest, the
creature must make a Strength challenge roll with 2 banes.
On a failure, the creature suffers the effects of stage
1 infection. While infected, the creature is diseased
and, each time it completes a rest, must make another
Strength challenge roll with 2 banes. Find the results of
the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from mind fire and becomes
immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature makes Will challenge rolls with 2 banes.
Stage 2 As stage 1, and the creature gains 1d6 Insanity.
If the creature becomes subject to madness, do not roll
on the Madness table. Instead, the creature becomes
subject to Violence.
Stage 3 As stage 1, and the creature gains 2d6 Insanity.
If the creature becomes subject to madness, do not roll
on the Madness table. Instead, the creature becomes
subject to Violence and rolls twice, using the lower
result, to end the madness effect.
Stage 4 The creature takes damage equal to its Health
and a mind fire slime slithers out from its nostrils. The
creature is hostile to all creatures and takes the next
available turn to attack the creature nearest to it.
Aftereffects The creature’s maximum amount of Insanity
is permanently reduced by 2.

--- PDF p. 4 ---
MIND FIRE SLIME

DIFFICULTY 5

Size 1/2 frightening ooze
Perception 10 (+0); sightless
Defense 8; Health 33; Insanity —; Corruption 0
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 8 (–2), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 6; climber, swimmer
Immune damage from disease; blinded, charmed, dazed,
diseased, frightened, grabbed, prone, stunned, and any
effect that would change its shape.
Infectious Any living creature of flesh and blood that
touches or is touched by the mind fire slime becomes
exposed to mind fire.
Confounding Thoughts The mind fire slime broadcasts
the thoughts of creatures whose brains it has devoured.
At the end of each round, each creature within short
range of the slime must succeed on a Will challenge roll
with 1 bane or gain 1 Insanity. A successful challenge roll
renders the creature immune to this slime’s confounding
thoughts until the creature completes a rest.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Pseudopod (melee) +1 with 3 boons (2d6)

Nerothian
Fungal Spores

Like the rot maiden, the nerothian fungus too has
a humanoid shape, but rather than attaining that
shape by growth, the form comes from the creature
victimized by its spores. Nerothian fungus thrives
when it grows in rotting meat, and from the inverted
caps that unfold all over the body waft millions
of spores drifting in the breeze and searching for
purchase on the body of a nearby creature.
So small are these motes that they can lodge in skin
pores and take root, tendrils spreading throughout the
body to control the host’s nervous system. After a few
days, the fungus makes its host into something like a
zombie, until the body finally gives out and dies.
Immolation Fire destroys the fungus’s spores
and thus the only real cure for this infestation is to
burn the victim alive or near enough that the spores
die while leaving the host creature a burned ruin.
A creature infected with the spores that becomes
incapacitated by damage from fire and at least half the
damage in its damage total comes from fire is cured of
the infection.

Nerothian Fungal Spores Effects
Infection A corpse of a creature that succumbed to the
spore infection emits spores that partially obscure a
sphere of space with a 5-yard radius centered on a
point in the corpse’s space. Any creature that enters the
area of spores becomes infected. A creature with fur
covering its body can roll a d20 and escapes infection
on a roll of 10 or higher. A creature infected in this way
suffers the stage 1 effects of the parasites 24 hours later.
Henceforth, whenever the infected creature completes a
rest, it must make a Strength challenge roll with 3 banes.
Find the results of the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from the nerothian fungal
spores and becomes immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature is diseased.
Stage 2 As stage 1, but the creature is also impaired and
slowed.
Stage 3 As stage 2, but whenever the creature gets a
failure on an attack roll or challenge roll, the creature
becomes controlled by the GM for 1d3 rounds.
Stage 4 The creature becomes a fungal thrall of its Size
and stops making Strength challenge rolls to fight the
infection. The creature remains a fungal thrall until it dies.
Apply the following template to the creature.

FUNGAL THRALL

DIFFICULTY REDUCE BY ONE

fungus
Perception 10 (+0); sightless
Insanity —; Corruption —
Intellect —, Will —
Speed 6
Immune asleep, blinded, dazed, deafened, fatigued,
frightened, stunned
Fungal Control Unless attacked, in which case it defends
itself, the fungal thrall takes a fast turn each round and
moves its Speed in a randomly determined direction.
Infectious Spores When a creature that can reach the
fungal thrall deals damage to it with a melee weapon,
the attacking creature must succeed on an Intellect
challenge roll or become infected with the spores as
described above.

MAGIC
Power 0
The creature loses all traditions and spells.
```

```text
The Astronomica
The Cult of the New God understood the peril the
Astronomica posed and thus moved to remove it from the
lands of the Empire. Dozens of incomplete copies, partially
transcribed from an authentic copy, went into the pyres,
as did several fabrications, books bearing the title but
filled with nonsense. The Cult managed to secure several
authentic, complete books and then burned them. One
copy, however, escaped their clutches: the original.
The Astromica’s size and bulk make concealing it difficult:
It weighs 30 pounds and measures 3 feet by 2 feet by 1
foot. Worse, anyone lugging it around feels as if some
liquid sloshes around inside, which makes it even more
cumbersome. Some kind of coral-like growth completely
covers the book, even the pages. A starfish is found on one
side. Twisting it to the right detaches it from the book’s
surface. Once free, a potential reader must place the
starfish over their face, at which point it becomes affixed
until removed. Removing it deals 1 damage as the starfish
grows quite comfortable and loses interest in independent
living. While the starfish is in place, the reader sees the
book open—no others do—to reveal a pool of water. Words
swim up in the pool and disappear when read. It takes 80
hours to read the book, and only by finishing it can one
gain its powers.
Dread Knowledge of the Sleeping God: You gain 1d3
Insanity, 3 Corruption, and you become cursed (as if by
a rank 7 spell). While cursed in this way, you become
impaired while you are not submerged in water.
Magical Secrets: You discover the Madness and Water
traditions if you have not discovered them already. If
you have, you learn a rank 0 spell from the tradition
instead. Details on the Madness tradition appear in
Occult Philosophy.
Awaken the Sleeping God: The book contains a ritual
to awaken the sleeping one. The ritual requires 100
gc worth of exotic ingredients, the participation of 8
people, and 24 hours of constant prayer and recitals
of the mystic words, all performed on the edge of
the Auroral Ocean. Upon finishing the ritual, each
participant takes 8d6 damage and gains Insanity equal
to their Will scores. Then, the seas froth as a demon
prince rises from the depths. (See The Hunger in the
Void, page 64, for rules.) The prince looks exactly like
the idol: a towering humanoid with a squid head and
a mass of writhing tentacles surrounding its beak. The
now awakened thing rampages across the countryside,
visiting death and destruction to everything in its path.

5

A Dark Tide Rises
The Seekers of the Sleeping God present a grave danger
to Rûl. They act to awaken their eldritch master, heedless
of the horrors doing so will unleash on the world. The
Sleeping God’s influence blinds them to the reality of
what their service will bring and to the ravages that
worshipping their master inflicts upon their flesh. You can
use the following campaign structure to create a series of
adventures featuring the cult. Each tier includes a Shadow
of the Demon Lord to describe the perilous conditions
brought on by the Hunger’s attention.

Stirrings in the Deep (Novice)
The orcs invade the Holy Kingdom. They butcher the
inhabitants, torture the priests, and sack the temples. A
strange group of people follow them, seemingly priests of
Oceanus. However the characters become involved, they
must contend with the priests who take some acolytes
prisoner and torture them for information concerning a
lost tome they call the Astronomica.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: Gray-green clouds blot out
the skies and remain. Sometimes, they swirl around.
One can see emerald lightning reach down to scorch the
earth. It rains two days out of every three.

Seaward Shenanigans (Expert)
After a merchant ship loaded with medical supplies never
reaches Freeport, the authorities hire the player characters
to find it and recover what they can. During the voyage, the
characters encounter storms, a kraken attack, and devotees
of a bizarre god peering into the deep to find their sleeping
master. The characters learn that the cultists attack ships
and take them to widen the range of their search.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: It now rains every day and
flooding becomes a problem. Worse, the raindrops
contain some slimy mucus that taints water. People who
drink the tainted water gain fishy mutations after 1d3
days.

The Dread Ritual (Master)
The cultists recover the Astronomica and locate the Sleeping
One. They gather to perform the ritual on a ship when
Tarterus hides from the night sky, and all the planets align
with Urth in a row. The characters learn about the attempt
and have 24 hours to stop the ritual before it finishes. The
group must track down the ship, deal with the various
guardians in their path, and thwart Kristane and the
demons he summons, or all is lost.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: The rains become
downpours. Sea levels rise, and most coastal cities
and settlements drown. Worse, mutated people run
amok through the countryside, screeching and hooting
prayers to the Sleeper.
```


## 71. Frayed Ends — quirks opcionais

**Fonte:** *Frayed Ends.pdf*  
**Cobertura:** PDF pp. 1–4. [OPCIONAL] [REGRA]

Procedimento: quando um personagem ganharia um quirk, usa-se 1d6 para selecionar uma das seis tabelas e depois 1d20 para determinar o quirk. O suplemento declara estas regras inteiramente opcionais.

```text
Frayed Ends offers a new way to show the cost of gaining
Insanity in Shadow of the Demon Lord. Normally, player
characters can rid themselves of Insanity by gaining quirks,
odd, compulsive behaviors that sometimes reflect the sources
of Insanity characters acquire. This supplement goes beyond
the rules in Shadow and the Unhinge the Mind Poisoned Pages
expansion by presenting six tables of quirks you can use to
relieve your mind of the madness you have endured. Rather
than working with the GM to determine your quirk, whenever
you would gain a quirk, roll a d6 and find the numbered table
matching the number you rolled. Then, roll a d20 to find the
quirk you gain.
Quirks acquired from these tables might be personality
disorders, delusions, or strange behaviors that manifest
under specific situations. To preserve the game’s grim
atmosphere, it’s important to include quirks gained when
roleplaying. In doing so, you demonstrate both the fragility
of the mortal mind as well as the horrid experiences you have
endured so far. As with all Poisoned Pages additions, the rules
in this booklet are entirely optional. Before introducing them
into your games, be sure to discuss them with your players
and Game Master to ensure all are interested in heightening
the tension at the table.

~Credits~

WRITING and Design:
Christi Bradford
editing AND Development: Robert J. Schwalb
Proofreading: Jay Spight
LAYOUT: kara hamilton
ILLUSTRATIONs: Matteo Spirito
with Britt Martin
Frayed Ends is ©2019 Schwalb Entertainment, LLC.
All rights reserved.

Schwalb Entertainment, and their associated logos
are trademarks of Schwalb Entertainment, LLC.
Schwalb Entertainment, LLC

PO Box #12548, Murfreesboro, TN 37129
info@schwalbentertainment.com www.schwalbentertainment.com
```

```text
burn with patriotic indignation and believe that they will,
like their ancestors before them, throw off the chains of

ordinary folk, engaged in any occupation and with their

As the membership swells and the Heirs’ popularity grows,
both Dolof Mylen and Cardinal Allora fear enemies might
infiltrate their ranks. It would be nice to think that everyone
who joined shared the same enthusiasm and dedication to
the cause, but the leaders know that the Cult of the New
God has spies everywhere and, worse, the sitting godqueen opposes their presence in Old Edene. To root out
the disloyal members and secret apologists for the New
God, the Heirs formed the Wyvern Eyes to serve as a spy
network.
Eyes have tattooed in the palm of their hands a green eye
with a slitted pupil, which they show to identify themselves
when needed. Most disguise themselves in ordinary
clothing so they can get close to hidden enemies and
```

## 74. Hired Help — hirelings, recrutamento e Loyalty

**Fonte:** *Hired Help.pdf*  
**Cobertura:** PDF pp. 2–6. [OPCIONAL] [REGRA] [CRIATURA]

Inclui Skill Rating, disponibilidade/preço, busca e contratação, secrets/complications, todos os sample hirelings, customização e o subsistema de Loyalty. Nomes de spells listados em stat blocks permanecem apenas como referências.

```text
--- PDF p. 2 ---
Hirelings

Seasoned adventures recognize the value of investing
in a few hirelings to attend to the mundane, day-today tasks. If you’ve sent a demon howling back into
the Void, having to keep your armor polished can feel
a bit anticlimactic. You have better things to do than
fumbling around with a torch, holding the horses’
reins, or looking for lodging the next time you blow
into Crossings. Unless you’re a skinflint, you’re bound
to at least be tempted by the folks out there who make
it their business to ease your way through the next
adventure. These folks, called hirelings, henchmen,
servants, lackeys, and less complementary names,
perform specific services in exchange for financial
remuneration.

Recruitment

Player characters might decide to part with some of
their hard-earned gold and silver to take on a few
hirelings to help out during their next adventure,
but where do they look to find such august persons?
Luckily, nearly every town and settlement plays host
to no shortage of individuals looking for work. And
one never has to go far to find suitable help, for these
potential hirelings flock to places where they might
find employment. A quick trip to the docks can elicit
a dozen or more offers to resolve all manner of needs,
from those of hauling and lifting, to those of a more
intimate nature. Similarly, hotels, high-class inns,
coaching stations, and other venues of a like kind
attract the hungry and eager.
The abundance of offers says little about the
quality of the individuals in search of pay. After all,
if they were competent, might they not already have
gainful employment? A discerning employer never
accepts the first offer and takes the time to conduct
a proper interview in order to ascertain the merits
and flaws of the hireling. Doing so weeds out those
with insurmountable defects and ensures one finds
qualified candidates able and willing to perform all
the functions of the job described.
This said, the number of prospective candidates
depends largely on the nature of the work and the
size of the community. Any yokel can be convinced to
hold a lantern for a few coins, but scholars of ancient
esoteric lore don’t often quarter in rude hamlets
on the thinly populated fringe of civilization’s vast
tapestry. Similarly, a seemingly qualified contender
for a difficult and dangerous job in some far-flung
village ought to raise alarms; such people don’t often
wind up in such places without good reason. It pays to
inquire into the interviewee’s history and references to
dodge avoidable shenanigans.

2

Skill and Availability
Each hireling has a skill rating, which determines
their availability and capabilities. The skill rating is
a number from 0 to 5, with 0 being unskilled and 5
being quite proficient. Skill rating 0 characters tend
to be laborers with little to no formal training. A
trained fighter might be skill rating 3 and a magicuser would be 5. The first table that follows shows
sample professions by skill rating, while the second
table shows availability and price using the scale
introduced in Shadow.

hunters, entertainers, and trappers

artisans, healers, and guards

the community size and their availability. When

skill level, secretly roll a d6 to see what they find
for each day spent looking in a community of the
appropriate size.
```
